rounds.text: Despite top-line expansion, the fundamental profitability and cash-generation profile of EMA Partners India Ltd deteriorates significantly across multiple metrics. Operating margins have collapsed by 13 percentage points, falling to 12% in the trailing twelve months from 25% three years prior, with the yearly trend consistently decreasing over the last four years [E22, E24]. This margin compression translates directly into severe cash burn, evidenced by a negative cash conversion of -0.08x, operating cash flow dropping to Rs -1 Cr, and free cash flow worsening to Rs -4 Cr for March 2026 [E26, E27, E28]. Concurrently, balance sheet leverage is rising sharply, with borrowings jumping from Rs 1 Cr to Rs 23 Cr by September 2026 [E31]. Capital efficiency also remains subdued, highlighted by a declining median return on equity of 9% over the last year and a flagged multi-year average of 12.1% [E21, E44], while working capital efficiency degrades as working capital days stretch from 41.5 to 65.9 days [E45]. Institutional confidence is visibly retreating alongside these strains, marked by negative institutional money flow, a reduction in foreign institutional ownership from 1.90% to 0.12%, and a flat 0.00% dividend yield despite repeated reported profits [E34, E36, E43]. conceded: [E15, E37]

A severe structural deterioration in profitability undermines the bull narrative, evidenced by operating margins collapsing by 13 percentage points to 12% in the TTM compared to three years earlier, alongside a continuous four-year yearly downward trend [E22, E24]. This margin compression coincides with a troubling deterioration in cash generation, resulting in negative operating cash flow of Rs -1 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -4 Cr for March 2026, translating to a poor cash conversion ratio of -0.08x [E26, E27, E28]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency is degrading as working capital days have stretched significantly from 41.5 days to 65.9 days [E45], while borrowings have jumped sharply to Rs 23 Cr in September 2026 from just Rs 1 Cr a year earlier [E31]. Institutional confidence is waning visibly through negative money flow and a 2.07 percentage point holding reduction, driven heavily by foreign institutions cutting their stake from 1.90% to 0.12% [E34, E36]. Conceded: the company trades at a reasonable P/E of 15.5x against a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 245 [E1, E37], and exhibits strong top-line growth with compounded sales expanding 74% in the trailing twelve months [E15].
